outcome: An effect without zone-specific text changes only permanents, leaving cards in graveyards and other zones untouched.
An effect asking for more than is possible does as much as it can, such as discarding only the single card in hand.
An as-though effect makes an action legal or illegal for its stated purpose only and the game is treated normally otherwise.
Two as-though effects combine so an action needing both conditions is legal.
Spending mana as though it were any type pays the cost without changing the cost or the mana actually spent.

note: Tells card authors that text must specify tie handling; no engine outcome of its own.
Introduces damage-source effects; the sub-rules carry the outcomes.

outcome: A damage-source shield applies to the next damage from the chosen source, whatever its kind, including a permanent spell and the permanent it becomes.
note: Names the source choice and its observable consequence.

outcome: A source-property shield rechecks the source at damage time, does not apply if the properties no longer match, and is not used up when it prevents or replaces nothing.
A static prevention or replacement effect keyed to a source property applies to matching permanents and to matching sources outside the battlefield.
